summary: Reads one line from a buffered file stream into a caller buffer: reads single bytes until newline (0x0A), the length limit a3 is exhausted, or the read fails; null-terminates the populated string and returns the buffer pointer, or returns 0 when no data was stored.

operations.description: If a2 (destination buffer) is NULL, return 0.
Read one byte from the buffered file stream into the buffer: BufferedFileReader(a1, v3, 1), where a1 is the file context held in field this+0.
Break the loop when the read returned != 1 (end of stream or failure).
Iterate reading bytes until capacity is exhausted (--v6 <= 0), a read fails, or the consumed byte is newline (0x0A).
Return 0 when no bytes were stored (a2 == v3) and capacity remains (v6 > 0); otherwise return a2, the pointer to the populated string.

clean_pseudocode: do { if (--left <= 0) break; if (BufferedFileReader(a1, cur, 1) != 1) break; } while (*cur++ != '\n');
